Dear Theo,

Re: balcony door lock, Flat 20, 110 Meadow Row, Northbridge, ZZ2 5ZZ (ref R/PM023-2)

The locksmith from Juniper Surveying tried to call this morning and left a voicemail (addressed to Freya Langley) to arrange a time to look at the balcony door lock. Could you please call them back, or reply to this email with a few days and times when someone can be in, so we can pass them on?

In the meantime, please keep the balcony door closed and secured as best you can, and let us know straight away if the door can't be closed or you feel the flat is not secure.

We'll check in with you and the locksmith tomorrow if no appointment has been arranged by then.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings

result.summary: The landlord approved attendance (event 6) and Juniper Surveying is already assigned (events 8–11). The locksmith has tried to reach the tenant to book a time (event 12), so the provider doesn't need a reply. I emailed the tenant asking them to call the locksmith back or send times they're available, and put the ticket on hold with a 1-day follow-up.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 6, Isaac: 'Yes that sounds like it needs sorting fairly soon' approves attendance. The contractor was assigned and told about the job (events 8–11), and the locksmith left a voicemail to book a time (event 12). Event 13 asks whether the provider needs a reply. It doesn't: the next step is the tenant and contractor agreeing a time. The voicemail went to 'Freya Langley', not Theo Ingram (the tenant on record), so I emailed Theo so the request reaches him, and set a hold so the job doesn't go quiet.

The landlord already approved attendance. Any repair cost will come back as a quote for approval. The contractor email says they must not proceed until approved.
Routine scheduling. The name difference can be cleared up with the tenant and doesn't change the decision.
